resources.string: Your DJI camera is paired with AeroCam. From now on, AeroCam can automatically reconnect to your camera.
Take a moment to set up your DJI camera for a great in-ride experience.
AeroCam can prevent your DJI cam from automatically going to standby.
Your camera turns off when its standby timer runs out—typically after 5 minutes—even while connected.
We highly recommend you enable this.
Keeping the camera awake uses battery. In our tests, we got around four hours of standby time with this feature enabled.
Let’s set up your DJI cam.
1. Set auto power off to %1$d minutes
Prevent standby prevents shutdown, but AeroCam needs to know the timer set on your camera.
I want a different standby time
Otherwise you’ll hear repeated clicks during your ride.
3. Turn off the display when locked (optional)
Now, when you lock your camera, the display turns off and saves precious battery.
Settings → Single Screen Preview (Scrn Off when Locked) → On
Choose the same Auto Power Off time here and on your DJI camera.
Next time you go for a ride, you can just:
This will turn off the display
Swipe down, then tap the lock: bottom row, second icon from the left.
Take photos, start recordings and add highlights at any time from your Karoo.
Prevent standby is off for now. Enable it in Settings or in a widget with the coffee icon.
Before using it, adjust a few settings on your DJI camera. You’ll find the steps in the FAQ.
AeroCam can add highlight markers to your recordings, or even automatically start a recording.
At the summit of a climb on your route
Automatically start recording when a selected trigger occurs.
Choose the threshold for this trigger.
Now all you need to do is add AeroCam widgets to your Karoo ride screen.
They come in various sizes. Try them out to find what suits you best.
Control your camera conveniently from your Karoo.
AeroCam automatically streams GPS, speed and elevation to your DJI camera to store in supported video recordings.
Use DJI Mimo to display this data, or try GPStitch, an open-source overlay editor.
My gosh, you’ve got some power.
Hey Pogačar, can you sign my hat?
On public roads, speed limits apply to you too 😉
Marks the ride start and end only when the camera is already recording. Pauses and resumes add no markers. Never starts a recording.
Choose a gradient. Speed is optional; enable it to require both conditions.
Enter speed from 1 to 80 km/h and gradient from +1 to +30%.
Enter speed from 40 to 80 km/h and gradient from −30 to −1%.
For example, start recording on a 5% descent or during a burst over 500 W.
Triggers tell AeroCam when to act.
Add a trigger that can start a video. Ride start/end markers only mark video that’s already recording.
You can change your triggers anytime in Settings → Automation.
Automation skipped. Set it up any time in Settings → Automation.
